1 &\text{if }\sum_{i\in\ell}\varepsilon_i\text{ is even},\\[2pt]
2 &\text{if }\sum_{i\in\ell}\varepsilon_i\text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
\]

The sum condition is

\[
\sum x_i\equiv |U|+\sum \varepsilon_i \equiv 0\pmod 3.
\]

We classify supports by their size using the Fano-plane orbit structure.

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
|U| & \text{type of support} & \#\text{ of such supports} & \text{valid assignments per support} & \text{total}\\ \hline
0 & - & 1 & 1 & 1\\
1 & - & 7 & 0 & 0\\
2 & \text{any pair} & 21 & 2 & 42\\
3 & \text{a line} & 7 & 0 & 0\\
3 & \text{non-collinear} & 28 & 2 & 56\\
4 & \text{complement of a line} & 7 & 6 & 42\\
4 & \text{complement of non-line} & 28 & 0 & 0\\
5 & \text{any }5\text{-set} & 21 & 8 & 168\\
6 & \text{any }6\text{-set} & 7 & 12 & 84\\
7 & \text{all points} & 1 & 0 & 0
\end{array}
\]

Brief justifications:

* **Size 2:** only \((1,2)\) and \((2,1)\) give sum \(0\).
* **Size 3 line:** the single surviving product is nonzero, so the second condition fails.
* **Size 3 non-collinear:** no product survives, and the sum condition forces all three entries to be equal, giving \(2\) choices.
* **Size 4, complement of a line:** this set contains no full line, so only the sum condition matters; exactly two entries must be \(2\), giving \(\binom42=6\).
* **Size 4, complement of a non-line:** it contains a line, whose product cannot be \(0\), so none work.
* **Size 5:** any two-point complement gives two intersecting lines sharing one point \(x\); the second condition forces the two line-products to differ, which yields \(8\) assignments per support.
* **Size 6:** the four surviving lines form the four faces of a tetrahedron; the second condition requires exactly two of them to have product \(2\). For each of the \(\binom42=6\) parity choices, exactly \(2\) of the \(8\) assignments satisfy the sum condition, giving \(12\) per support.
* **Size 7:** all entries nonzero. The sum condition requires exactly two or five \(2\)’s. With two \(2\)’s, four line-products are \(2\) and three are \(1\), so \(S\equiv2\). With five \(2\)’s, three line-products are \(2\) and four are \(1\), so \(S\equiv1\). Thus none work.

\[
1+42+56+42+168+84 = 393.
